audience: Indie founders evaluating small workflow tools
grounding: Explicit fictional decision hypotheses; no demographic or human-fidelity claims
context: Browsing short muted product demos on a phone. Each full clip lasts eight seconds; only the current segment is visible. No urgent purchase is required. There is no quota to watch, skip, agree or disagree.

card.goal: Find a useful improvement without spending scarce attention learning a tool.
card.knowledge: Comfortable with ordinary apps, unfamiliar with text-processing jargon.
tradeoffs: Can accept a simple visible result without a technical mechanism explanation
Will miss a useful tool if its relevance takes too long to become clear
Can wait when an early payoff makes the remaining explanation worthwhile
stop_conditions: Opening remains abstract or hard to understand

card.goal: Judge whether a workflow claim is technically credible and worth investigating.
card.knowledge: Understands text transformations, repeatability and edge cases.
priorities: Distinguish a claim from observable evidence
tradeoffs: Will spend attention on a concrete demonstration even when its opening is understated
Technical language is acceptable when it communicates something precise
Polish and novelty do not compensate for absent evidence
stop_conditions: No way to inspect what changed or why

card.goal: Improve a workflow without disclosing potentially sensitive working material.
card.knowledge: Understands local versus hosted processing and the uncertainty of absent data-handling information.
tradeoffs: Accepts extra steps to keep material local
A convenient hosted operation can be unacceptable for this use case
Does not assume a tool is local when the clip is silent about it
stop_conditions: The proposed workflow sends working material to an external service without a suitable alternative

card.goal: Remove repetitive work and reduce the actions required for routine non-sensitive material.
card.knowledge: Comfortable using hosted productivity services for this non-sensitive task.
tradeoffs: Can accept disclosed hosted processing for non-sensitive material
Local processing is welcome but does not justify substantial friction here
A real time saving matters more than unusual interaction design
stop_conditions: The tool adds work without a useful payoff

card.goal: Adopt a predictable workflow without risking loss of existing work.
card.knowledge: Maintains repeatable work routines and notices destructive changes and recovery behavior.
tradeoffs: Will accept a slower workflow if it is reversible
An attractive result is insufficient when recovery is unclear
A familiar interaction has value but is not automatically better
stop_conditions: Changes overwrite working material without a recovery path

card.goal: Discover interesting ways to interact with tools and learn whether they open up new possibilities.
card.knowledge: Technically curious and comfortable experimenting on disposable sample material.
tradeoffs: Will try a different interaction even when a familiar one already works
Can accept rough edges on disposable samples
Novelty alone is insufficient if the operation cannot be understood or tried
stop_conditions: The clip offers only spectacle with no understandable interaction or result

card.goal: Decide whether this workflow tool looks relevant and worth a little more attention.
tradeoffs: Weigh the whole clip without an assigned strong specialty preference
stop_conditions: Insufficient apparent usefulness to justify continuing
